title: Codebase Review Findings
description: Structured source of truth for a codebase review. Both HTML reports (founder + technical) render from this file. Diffing two of these files across time produces the delta/version view.

meta.description: Provenance stamp. Makes each report traceable to an exact state of the code.

commitSha.description: Full or short SHA the review was run against.

reviewDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Ask the user or read from git; never fabricate.

scopeExcluded.description: Explicit 'not reviewed / out of scope' list. Required for honesty; empty array is not acceptable without justification.

featureInventory.description: Rollup for the featureInventory[] array. Present whenever that array is.

count.description: Rows emitted. The denominator for any percentage stated anywhere.

stateCounts.description: Computed rollup. implemented + partial + uiOnly MUST equal count.

grainNote.description: One sentence on the lens that produced this list, so a reader knows what they are comparing their own understanding against. See SKILL.md 'Feature grain'.

headline.description: One sentence, founder voice, carrying the counts AND the denominator. Rendered in the founder report. Required when featureInventory[] exists.

scorecard.description: Top-of-report traffic lights. Keep to ~6 dimensions so a founder gets the picture in 15 seconds.

score.description: Per rubric.md. Enables comparison across versions.

businessMeaning.description: One plain-language sentence a non-engineer understands.

trend.description: vs previous review, if one exists.

executiveSummary.description: 3-6 sentences, plain language, zero jargon. What this system is, what state it's in, the single most important thing to know.

deltas.description: Populated only when a previous findings.json exists. Drives the 'Since last review' block.

resolved.description: Finding ids or titles closed since last review.

changed.description: Notable drift: architecture, dependencies, scope changes.

capabilityMap.description: The direct answer to 'we don't know what the code does': each user-facing capability mapped to where it lives.

plainLanguage.description: What it does, for a non-engineer.

codeLocations.description: Files/dirs that implement it, e.g. src/components/msp-onboarding/.

featureIds.description: featureInventory[] ids rolling up to this capability. Every inventory row belongs to exactly one capability; a capability with an empty array is a bug in the inventory.

featureInventory.description: The reviewer's perception of the product's user-facing features and flows, derived from code. The fine-grained expansion of capabilityMap. NOT a canonical registry: no external list is supplied, so there is no right answer about what counts as a feature — see SKILL.md 'Feature grain'. Projects to feature-inventory.csv, which a revenue owner enriches offline. Nothing they do with it returns to the review.

featureId.description: Sequential within this review, prefix 'FI-' (e.g. FI-001). Carried forward from a prior review when a row is recognizably the same feature, as a reader convenience. Not a contract: no high-water mark, no append-only invariant.

kind.description: feature = a discrete thing a user can do. flow = a multi-step path across features (e.g. need -> RFP -> award -> SOW). Flows are frequently what gets positioned, so they earn rows of their own.

name.description: Short name a non-engineer would recognize.

plainLanguage.description: What it does, for a non-engineer. One or two sentences. Must stand alone — this is read in a spreadsheet, away from the reports.

area.description: Product area from the code's own structure (route group, directory). NOT a sales category.

capability.description: Name of the capabilityMap[] entry this rolls up to.

state.description: implemented = works end to end. partial = some of it real, some not. ui-only = screen renders from mock or sample data, no working backend.

evidence.description: Cite-or-assume applies per row. 'partial' cites both the working part and the gap; 'ui-only' cites the mock or sample-data source.

roleMatrix.description: Internal roles/permissions if present. role -> allowed actions -> data scope.

architecture.description: The technical report renders a deep-dive from this: tech stack, multiple diagrams, cross-cutting concerns, and a feature x persona matrix. Aim for the depth of a standalone architecture report.

plainLanguage.description: Plain-language description of the pieces (no metaphors; see SKILL.md Voice).

techStack.description: Layer-by-layer stack: framework, language, styling, data layer, state, tooling, etc. Rendered as a table.

diagrams.description: Several complementary views, each a titled Mermaid diagram. Prefer at least: a system-context graph, a layered/dependency flowchart, a persona/route map, and a cross-actor lifecycle sequence. MERMAID GOTCHAS: never put ';' inside a sequenceDiagram message (it is a statement separator); never start a flowchart node label with '[/' (parses as a parallelogram); validate before shipping.

description.description: One line on what the diagram shows.

mermaid.description: Valid Mermaid source, or ASCII fallback.

diagram.description: DEPRECATED single-diagram field; prefer diagrams[]. Kept for back-compat.

crossCutting.description: Concerns that span personas/modules (payments, AI, verification, state management, design system, etc.). Rendered as a table.

detail.description: How it works and where it lives (cite modules).

featureMatrix.description: Feature x persona grid showing what each role can do with each feature. Adapt columns to the system's actual roles.

additionalProperties.description: One column per role, e.g. po/msp/admin; value is what that role does (or '—').

externalDependencies.description: Third-party services the system relies on (Stripe, auth, DB, etc.).

diagram.description: Mermaid ER diagram source or ASCII.

storage.description: DB table, localStorage key, in-memory module, etc.

workflows.description: Extracted user/system flows. Double as seeds for how-to documentation.

aiProvenance.description: Signals relevant when code was written with AI assistance. Not an accusation; a scrutiny map.

risky.description: High-impact but higher-risk changes; flag clearly.

auditMappings.description: Optional: map findings to a compliance framework for the audit-package output profile.

limitations.description: What could not be verified and why. Required for trust.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. SEC-01. Reused across versions so deltas can track it.

businessImpact.description: REQUIRED. 'What this means for you' in plain language: cost, risk, customer impact, or timeline.

evidence.description: Cite-or-assume rule: every finding needs at least one evidence ref OR basis='inferred' with justification.

basis.description: documented = stated in code/docs; inferred = the reviewer's deduction.
